messages:
Lena Ortiz: I'm iterating on a more declarative autoscale policy for dedicated GPU pools to handle noisy neighbor bursts. Proposal: policy document defines three independent axes - smoothing window, emergency fastpath, and per-tenant burst caps. Thoughts?

Samir Gupta: Sounds sensible. How do we expose the policy to operators? CRD or control plane push?

Lena Ortiz: Prefer control-plane push + immutable policy versions. Operator caches a version and reports applied hash back. Avoids large CR churn and lets us do staged rollouts.

Diane Park: We should include viability checks in the control plane before pushing (e.g., ensure pool has at least X headroom for requested burst_factor). Reject obvious bad configs.

Ashok Rao: Fastpath detail: allow immediate admits when free_slots >= free_threshold OR when queue_depth spike lasts < spike_window_ms but rate_of_change > slope_threshold. That prevents both over-admit and under-prewarm.

Samir Gupta: Also add a safety cap per host/slot so a single tenant can't steal warmers. Per-tenant token bucket that refills on longer windows.

Lena Ortiz: Agree. Metrics to add: `policy_applied_version`, `admit_decision{admit|fastpath|delayed|reject}`, `tenant_burst_usage`. Dashboards will help validate config impact.

deploy-bot: rollout 1810000020: autoscale-policy-v2 applied to canary cluster

Diane Park: Let's run three synthetic scenarios: steady-state, forecast-dropout, rapid microbursts. Capture percent delayed vs rejected and 95th latency. Share results here and we can iterate on defaults.

Lena Ortiz: I'll post the test harness and default policy draft after lunch. Thanks all.
